subject: technology-sp
description: Technology Senior Phase (Grades 7–9). CAPS-aligned. Four content strands done every grade (Structures, Mechanical Systems & Control, Electrical Systems & Control, Processing) plus the Design Process & graphics. All skills open once the grade is selected (gate NONE). Practical/making work is reframed into tap-only knowledge questions. Drawing-heavy skills flagged image_dependent carry held image-only questions until art exists.

levels.title: Grade 7 — Technology
levels.description: Grade 7 Technology (CAPS Senior Phase). Four content strands — Structures, Mechanical Systems, Electrical Systems and Processing — plus the Design Process and graphics, taught across the year.

tiers.title: Design Process & Graphics · Term 1
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T1 — Design Process & Graphics. Design process & graphics.

atomic_skills.title: What is Technology?
atomic_skills.description: What Technology means, its scope, and the careers in the world of work that use it.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "What is Technology?".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Technology means using knowledge, skills and resources to solve people's real problems.

atomic_skills.title: The design process (IDMEC)
atomic_skills.description: The five stages of the design process: Investigate, Design, Make, Evaluate and Communicate.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The design process (IDMEC)".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The design process: Investigate, Design, Make, Evaluate, Communicate.

atomic_skills.title: Design considerations & fitness-for-purpose
atomic_skills.description: Judging a design by who it is for, whether it works, cost, safety, ergonomics and looks.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Design considerations & fitness-for-purpose".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Fit-for-purpose asks: who is it for, will it do the job, is it safe, does it look good?

atomic_skills.title: Graphical communication & line types
atomic_skills.description: The purpose of drawings and the line conventions: outlines, construction lines, hidden detail, scale and dimensioning.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Graphical communication & line types".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Drawings use different lines: dark outlines, feint construction lines and dashed hidden detail.

atomic_skills.title: Drawing techniques: sketch, oblique, perspective
atomic_skills.description: Free-hand sketching, 2D working drawings of one face, 3D oblique at 45°, and single-vanishing-point perspective.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Drawing techniques: sketch, oblique, perspective".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sketches, flat working drawings and 3D drawings each show an object a different way.

atomic_skills.title: Purpose & classification of structures
atomic_skills.description: What structures do (contain, support, protect, span) and natural versus man-made structures.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Purpose & classification of structures".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A structure contains, supports, protects or spans; it can be natural or man-made.

atomic_skills.title: Types of structures: shell, frame, solid
atomic_skills.description: The three types of structures — shell, frame and solid — with everyday examples.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Types of structures: shell, frame, solid".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Three structure types: shell (hollow), frame (bars joined) and solid (one mass).

atomic_skills.title: Stiffening & reinforcing
atomic_skills.description: Making materials and structures stiffer by tubing, folding and triangulation.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Stiffening & reinforcing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: You can stiffen materials by folding, rolling into tubes, or triangulating a frame.

atomic_skills.title: Frame structures & stability
atomic_skills.description: Frame structures (towers, pylons) and what makes a structure stable — base size and centre of gravity.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Frame structures & stability".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A wide base and a low centre of gravity make a structure stable and hard to topple.

tiers.title: Mechanical Systems & Control · Term 1
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T1 — Mechanical Systems & Control. Mechanical systems & control.

atomic_skills.title: Levers & mechanical advantage
atomic_skills.description: First-, second- and third-class levers, and how the pivot position gives a mechanical advantage.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Levers & mechanical advantage".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A lever's class depends on where the fulcrum, load and effort are placed.

atomic_skills.title: Linkages in tools
atomic_skills.description: Linked levers in everyday tools — scissors, pliers, punches, staplers, tweezers.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Linkages in tools".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Linked levers join two levers so they work together, like the blades of scissors.

atomic_skills.title: Pneumatics & hydraulics
atomic_skills.description: Transferring force through air (pneumatic) and liquid (hydraulic) systems using syringes.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Pneumatics & hydraulics".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pneumatics use air; hydraulics use liquid; both push force along a tube.

atomic_skills.title: Cranks & pulleys
atomic_skills.description: The crank as an adapted second-class lever, and the pulley as a wheel and axle.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Cranks & pulleys".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A crank turns round motion into back-and-forth; a pulley is a wheel turning on an axle.

tiers.title: Electrical Systems & Control · Term 3
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T3 — Electrical Systems & Control. Electrical systems & control.

atomic_skills.title: Magnetism & magnetic materials
atomic_skills.description: Permanent magnets (bar, horseshoe) and which materials a magnet attracts.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Magnetism & magnetic materials".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Magnets attract some metals (iron, steel, nickel) but not non-metals or copper and aluminium.

atomic_skills.title: Simple electric circuits & symbols
atomic_skills.description: A simple circuit with a cell, switch, conductor and an output, drawn with correct symbols.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Simple electric circuits & symbols".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A circuit needs a power source, a conductor, a switch and an output like a bulb or buzzer.

atomic_skills.title: Electromagnets
atomic_skills.description: Making an electromagnet by coiling insulated wire around an iron core, and switching it on and off.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Electromagnets".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An electromagnet is wire coiled around an iron core; it is magnetic only while current flows.

tiers.title: Processing, Society & Environment · Term 4
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T4 — Processing, Society & Environment. Processing, society & environment.

atomic_skills.title: Processing food
atomic_skills.description: Processing food into useful, nutritious meals and the sequence of preparing a food item.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Processing food".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Processing changes raw ingredients into a useful product, like turning flour into bread.

atomic_skills.title: Materials & textiles
atomic_skills.description: Properties of materials and textiles, including waterproofing and burning characteristics.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Materials & textiles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Different materials and textiles suit different jobs because of their properties.

atomic_skills.title: Indigenous technology
atomic_skills.description: Materials and building techniques used by indigenous people — local, appropriate, environmentally friendly.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Indigenous technology".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Indigenous builders use local materials that are appropriate and kind to the environment.

atomic_skills.title: Impact & bias in technology
atomic_skills.description: How technology affects society and the environment, recycling, and bias for or against groups.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Impact & bias in technology".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Technology can help or harm people and the environment, and can favour some groups over others.

levels.title: Grade 8 — Technology
levels.description: Grade 8 Technology (CAPS Senior Phase). Four content strands — Structures, Mechanical Systems, Electrical Systems and Processing — plus the Design Process and graphics, taught across the year.

tiers.title: Design Process & Graphics · Term 1
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T1 — Design Process & Graphics. Graphics & drawing.

atomic_skills.title: Graphics conventions
atomic_skills.description: Drawing conventions — centre lines (chain dash-dot), scaling up and down, dimensioning in mm.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Graphics conventions".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Conventions like centre lines, scaling and dimensions in mm keep drawings clear and standard.

atomic_skills.title: Isometric & two-point perspective
atomic_skills.description: Isometric drawing on a 30° grid and double-vanishing-point perspective with colour and shading.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Isometric & two-point perspective".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Isometric uses a slanted grid; two-point perspective uses two vanishing points for realism.

atomic_skills.title: Developments (nets)
atomic_skills.description: Drawing the development (net) of an opened container that folds up into a 3D shape.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Developments (nets)".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A development (net) is the flat shape that folds up into a box or container.

atomic_skills.title: Frame members & roof trusses
atomic_skills.description: Structural members of wood and steel roof trusses — king/queen post, strut, tie, rafter, tie beam.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Frame members & roof trusses".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A roof truss is built from struts, ties, rafters and posts, each doing a job.

atomic_skills.title: Forces acting on members
atomic_skills.description: The forces that act on structural members — tension, compression, shear, torsion and bending.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Forces acting on members".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Five forces act on materials: tension (pull), compression (push), shear, torsion (twist) and bending.

atomic_skills.title: Structures that span space
atomic_skills.description: Ways of spanning a gap — beams and girders, suspension and cable-stayed bridges, arches and cantilevers.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Structures that span space".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Beams, arches, cantilevers and bridges each span a gap in a different way.

atomic_skills.title: Structural failure
atomic_skills.description: The three main ways structures fail — fracture (strength), bending (stiffness) and toppling (stability).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Structural failure".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Structures fail by fracturing (too weak), bending (not stiff) or toppling (not stable).

tiers.title: Mechanical Systems & Control · Term 3
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T3 — Mechanical Systems & Control. Mechanical systems & control.

atomic_skills.title: Simple mechanisms: wedge, wheel & axle
atomic_skills.description: Simple machines — the wedge (inclined plane, blade) and the wheel and axle.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Simple mechanisms: wedge, wheel & axle".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A wedge and a wheel-and-axle are simple machines that make work easier.

atomic_skills.title: Gears: counter-rotation & idlers
atomic_skills.description: How two meshed spur gears counter-rotate, and how an idler gear synchronises rotation.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Gears: counter-rotation & idlers".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Meshed gears turn opposite ways; an idler gear between them makes them turn the same way.

atomic_skills.title: Gear ratios: velocity & force
atomic_skills.description: Gear ratios — how different gear sizes trade speed for force (velocity ratio and force ratio).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Gear ratios: velocity & force".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A small gear driving a big one cuts speed but increases force; the opposite raises speed.

atomic_skills.title: Cams & cranks
atomic_skills.description: Mechanisms that change the direction of movement — the cam and the crank turn rotary into reciprocating motion.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Cams & cranks".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A cam and a crank both change round motion into up-and-down (reciprocating) motion.

atomic_skills.title: Mechanical advantage calculations
atomic_skills.description: Calculating mechanical advantage for levers and gears using ratios (load/effort, tooth ratios) — no moments.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Mechanical advantage calculations".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort, worked out with simple ratios.

atomic_skills.title: Systems diagrams
atomic_skills.description: Analysing a mechanical system as input → process → output, e.g. a bicycle gear system.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Systems diagrams".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Every system has an input, a process and an output.

tiers.title: Electrical Systems & Control · Term 4
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T4 — Electrical Systems & Control. Electrical systems & control.

atomic_skills.title: Circuit components & symbols
atomic_skills.description: Circuit components grouped as input, output and control devices, with their correct symbols.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Circuit components & symbols".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Devices are input (cell), output (lamp, buzzer, motor) or control (switch).

atomic_skills.title: Cells & energy sources
atomic_skills.description: Electrochemical cells, series versus parallel batteries, and solar (photovoltaic) cells.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Cells & energy sources".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cells store energy; series batteries give more voltage, parallel ones last longer.

atomic_skills.title: Generating electricity for the nation
atomic_skills.description: Generating electricity — thermal, hydroelectric and wind — and the national grid with transformers.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Generating electricity for the nation".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Power stations (coal, water, wind) feed the national grid through step-up and step-down transformers.

atomic_skills.title: Ohm's law (qualitative) & logic gates
atomic_skills.description: Ohm's law qualitatively (more cells, more current) and AND/OR logic gates with truth tables.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Ohm's law (qualitative) & logic gates".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: More cells means more current; AND and OR logic gates decide when a circuit switches on.

tiers.title: Processing, Society & Environment · Term 2
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T2 — Processing, Society & Environment. Processing, society & environment.

atomic_skills.title: Materials & the environment
atomic_skills.description: How new and improved materials replace natural ones, and biodegradable materials.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Materials & the environment".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: New materials can replace natural ones; biodegradable materials break down safely.

atomic_skills.title: Recycling & packaging design
atomic_skills.description: Recycling paper and cardboard, and designing packaging suited to a product.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Recycling & packaging design".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Packaging protects a product; paper and plastic can be recycled into new products.

atomic_skills.title: Impact of technology
atomic_skills.description: The positive and negative impacts of technology and ways to counteract the negative effects.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Impact of technology".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Technology has good and bad impacts; we can design to reduce the harm.

atomic_skills.title: Mining impact, indigenous mining & bias
atomic_skills.description: The environmental impact of mining, indigenous iron-age mining, and bias such as gender bias.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Mining impact, indigenous mining & bias".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mining brings wealth but harms the environment, and technology can carry bias against groups.

levels.title: Grade 9 — Technology
levels.description: Grade 9 Technology (CAPS Senior Phase). Four content strands — Structures, Mechanical Systems, Electrical Systems and Processing — plus the Design Process and graphics, taught across the year.

tiers.title: Design Process & Graphics · Term 1
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T1 — Design Process & Graphics. Graphics & drawing.

atomic_skills.title: First-angle orthographic projection
atomic_skills.description: Showing a 3D object as three flat views — front, top and side — in first-angle orthographic projection.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "First-angle orthographic projection".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Orthographic projection shows an object as three flat views: front, top and side.

atomic_skills.title: Working drawings & design problems
atomic_skills.description: Drawing a working plan that actually solves a problem (e.g. a stair and ramp), to scale with dimensions.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Working drawings & design problems".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A working drawing must really solve the problem — neat is not enough if it won't work.

atomic_skills.title: Artistic & exploded assembly drawing
atomic_skills.description: Artistic single-VP perspective for realism and exploded assembly views showing how parts fit.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Artistic & exploded assembly drawing".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An exploded view shows the parts pulled apart to reveal how they fit together.

atomic_skills.title: Forces: static, dynamic & loads
atomic_skills.description: Static and dynamic forces, even and uneven loads, and how members resist tension, compression and torsion.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Forces: static, dynamic & loads".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Forces can be static (still) or dynamic (moving); loads can be even or uneven.

atomic_skills.title: Strength of materials & cross-sections
atomic_skills.description: How a material's cross-section (I-beam, angle iron, tube) helps it resist forces and save material.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Strength of materials & cross-sections".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A material's cross-section, like an I-beam, helps it resist bending without extra weight.

atomic_skills.title: Properties of construction materials
atomic_skills.description: Properties of construction materials — density, hardness, stiffness, flexibility and corrosion resistance.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Properties of construction materials".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Materials differ in density, hardness, stiffness, flexibility and how much they corrode.

atomic_skills.title: Costing & the tender process
atomic_skills.description: Costing a real solution (materials and labour) and the tender process, including ethics.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Costing & the tender process".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A tender is a priced offer to do a job; costing includes both materials and labour.

tiers.title: Mechanical Systems & Control · Term 2
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T2 — Mechanical Systems & Control. Mechanical systems & control.

atomic_skills.title: Hydraulics & Pascal's principle
atomic_skills.description: Pascal's principle, compressible versus incompressible fluids, and the hydraulic press and jack.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Hydraulics & Pascal's principle".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pascal's principle: pressure spreads equally through a liquid; cylinder sizes change the force.

atomic_skills.title: Pulleys & mechanical control devices
atomic_skills.description: Fixed and moveable pulleys, block and tackle, and control devices — ratchet and pawl, brakes, cleat.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Pulleys & mechanical control devices".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Moveable pulleys and block-and-tackle multiply force; ratchets and brakes control motion.

atomic_skills.title: Advanced gears
atomic_skills.description: Bevel gears, rack-and-pinion and worm gear systems and what each is used for.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Advanced gears".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Bevel gears turn a corner; rack-and-pinion gives straight motion; a worm gear slows speed a lot.

atomic_skills.title: Integrated systems
atomic_skills.description: Machines that combine at least two of mechanical, electrical and hydraulic/pneumatic sub-systems.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Integrated systems".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Real machines often combine mechanical, electrical and hydraulic or pneumatic systems.

tiers.title: Electrical Systems & Control · Term 3
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T3 — Electrical Systems & Control. Electrical & electronic systems.

atomic_skills.title: Ohm's law (quantitative)
atomic_skills.description: Ohm's law as V = I × R, and calculating resistance, voltage or current from the other two.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Ohm's law (quantitative)".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ohm's law: V = I × R, so any one value can be found from the other two.

atomic_skills.title: Resistor colour codes
atomic_skills.description: Reading the value of a resistor from its coloured bands and the tolerance band.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Resistor colour codes".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Coloured bands on a resistor give its value in ohms, with the last band a tolerance.

atomic_skills.title: Electronic components
atomic_skills.description: Diodes, LEDs, NPN transistors (switch and amplifier) and capacitors and what each does.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Electronic components".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A diode lets current flow one way; a transistor switches or amplifies; a capacitor stores charge.

atomic_skills.title: Sensors
atomic_skills.description: Sensors as input devices — LDR (light), thermistor (heat) and touch/moisture detectors.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Sensors".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sensors change their resistance with light (LDR), heat (thermistor) or moisture.

atomic_skills.title: Switches & circuit logic
atomic_skills.description: Manual switches (push, SPST, SPDT, DPDT) and series (AND) versus parallel (OR) circuit logic.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Switches & circuit logic".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Switches in series make AND logic; switches in parallel make OR logic.

atomic_skills.title: Simple electronic circuits
atomic_skills.description: Recognising simple electronic circuits that combine an LED, resistor, sensor, transistor or capacitor.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Simple electronic circuits".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Electronic circuits combine components like an LED, resistor and sensor to do a job.

tiers.title: Processing, Society & Environment · Term 4
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T4 — Processing, Society & Environment. Processing.

atomic_skills.title: Preserving metals
atomic_skills.description: Protecting metals from corrosion by painting, galvanising and electroplating.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Preserving metals".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Metals are protected from rusting by painting, galvanising (zinc) or electroplating.

atomic_skills.title: Preserving food
atomic_skills.description: Preserving food by storing grain, pickling, and drying and/or salting.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Preserving food".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Food is preserved by storing it dry, pickling it, or drying and salting it.

atomic_skills.title: Plastics: types & properties
atomic_skills.description: Types of plastics, their identification codes and properties, and thermoplastics versus thermosets.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Plastics: types & properties".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remoulded; thermosets stay hard.

atomic_skills.title: Recycling plastics
atomic_skills.description: Reduce-reuse-recycle, remanufacturing waste plastic into pellets, and a plastics recycling system.
